decisions.reason: Untitled quote from Glazer 1956 that Wallman (1858) reported the first colloid/'paraphyseal' cyst; duplicate of R002, the label is Glazer's, 1858 predates the paraphysis-cyst concept and no histogenesis is given.

Wallmann 1858 autopsy report of a third-ventricle colloid cyst and a choroid plexus lipoma; first description only, no paraphyseal or histogenetic argument (first-description date is citable via Glazer 1956).
De Graaf 1886 title concerns epiphysis (pineal/parietal eye) development in amphibians and reptiles; predates the term paraphysis (Selenka 1891); nothing indicates paraphysis content (metadata only).

Selenka 1891 (Das Stirnorgan der Wirbeltiere) is the classically credited first identification of the paraphysis in the chick (Dexter 1902); link of Dexter's ref (12) to this exact paper is inferred, content not seen.

Burckhardt 1892 Protopterus CNS monograph where the lungfish roof structure was named 'coronarium' (later paraphysis per Studnicka, dorsal sac per Tsuneki); origin of the contested lungfish terminology.

Burckhardt 1894 on homologies of the diencephalic roof in lower vertebrates (epiphysis, paraphysis, dorsal sac per finder); classical homology paper, paraphysis coverage inferred from citations, content unverified.

Burckhardt 1894 companion on reptiles and birds; cited for showing the paraphysis in a crow embryo as a small diverticulum like that of Petromyzon (identity of Dexter's ref (3) with this paper inferred).
Hill 1894 on the epiphysis of teleosts and Amia; title confined to the pineal; no indication of paraphysis content (metadata only).

Sorensen 1894 comparative study of epiphysis and diencephalic roof; cited by Gladstone and Wakeley for the dorsal sac and paraphysis of the alligator, so a classical roof/paraphysis description; content unverified.
Leydig 1895 on Zirbel (pineal) and parietal organs; title not about the paraphysis, 'Stirnorgan' overlap is only a terminological possibility (metadata only).
Studnicka 1895 'Zur Anatomie der sog. Paraphyse des Wirbelthiergehirns': title names the paraphysis; content unverified (metadata only).
Melchers 1899 on rudimentary brain appendages of the gecko (Epi-, Para- und Hypophyse); title names the paraphysis; cited as classical in the 2025 gecko paper; content unverified.

Stemmler 1900 dissertation on development of the diencephalic-roof appendages of the gecko (subtitle reportedly covers epiphysis, parietal organ and paraphysis); cited in the 2025 gecko paraphysis paper; exact title wording unverified.
Dexter 1902, development of the paraphysis in the fowl; first dedicated avian paraphysis embryology paper with literature review (D'Erchia, Selenka, Burckhardt).
Dexter's fowl paraphysis paper as transcribed on the UNSW wiki (excerpt gives cavity continuous with forebrain and thickening wall); duplicate of R014 (dated 1903 in the transcription).

Studnicka 1905 'Die Parietalorgane': excerpt records his argument that Burckhardt's lungfish coronarium should be called paraphysis, a key terminology/homology step; chapter also a standard comparative reference.
Warren 1905, development of the paraphysis and pineal region in Necturus; title names paraphysis; excerpt compares the paraphysis in adult amphibian brains (Osborn).
Chiarugi 1906 on the paraphyseal region of the telencephalon in Torpedo ocellata embryos; title names the paraphyseal region (OCR-garbled), content unverified.

Johnston 1909 forebrain vesicle morphology: defines roof plate, lamina terminalis/supraneuroporica and tela chorioidea, the framework that locates the paraphysis (ontogeny/anatomy); no paraphysis passage seen in the snippet.
Untitled citation of Sjovall 1909 as first proposing a paraphyseal origin of colloid cysts (duplicate of R021); explicit historiographic anchor for the paraphyseal hypothesis.
Sjovall 1909 'Ependymcyste embryonalen Charakters (Paraphyse?) im dritten Hirnventrikel': title names the paraphysis; origin of the paraphyseal cyst concept.
Whole Keibel and Mall Manual of Human Embryology; no paraphysis passage located; the relevant nervous-system chapter (Streeter, R027) is screened separately.
Reese 1910, development of the alligator brain: the paraphysis and hypophysis; title names paraphysis; crocodilian ontogeny; content unverified.

Dendy 1911 tuatara pineal organs 'and adjacent parts of the brain': title ambiguous, no excerpt; resolve by checking whether the monograph describes the paraphysis/dorsal sac and velum of Sphenodon (likely, but unseen).
Warren 1911 'Paraphysis and Pineal Region in Reptilia': title names paraphysis; reptile developmental study (duplicate of R026).
Warren 1911 development of the paraphysis and pineal region in Reptilia; title names paraphysis; telencephalic origin anterior to the velum (duplicate of R025).

Streeter 1912 human nervous-system embryology: excerpt records homologising the anterior choroidal pouch with the paraphysis of lower vertebrates (human ontogeny/homology); second-hand quote via Bailey 1916, paraphysis is not the chapter's subject.

Bailey 1916 human forebrain roof plate and lateral choroid plexus: roof region from which the paraphysis arises, disputes paraphysis identifications in man (human ontogeny); excerpt itself silent on paraphysis.

Choroid plexus morphogenesis in the turtle Chrysemys; reported to cite Warren's paraphysis work, so it locates telencephalon-medium plexus relative to the paraphysis (reptile anatomy/ontogeny); authorship and paraphysis content unverified.

Warren 1917 'On the pineal region in human embryos': Warren's 'pineal region' may include the paraphysis, but title names only the pineal; resolve by checking the UNSW transcription for paraphysis statements in human embryos.

Warren 1917 development of the paraphysis and pineal region in mammalia: distinct paraphysis in sheep embryos 21-48 mm, rudimentary and inconstant in humans, arising from the roof plate in front of the velum.
Tilney and Warren 1919 monograph on the pineal body; title pineal-focused; no evidence of paraphysis content (metadata only).
Kappers 1920-21 general comparative nervous system treatise; no paraphysis statement identified; content is superseded by the 1936 treatise (R041/R042).

Hines 1921 defines the human telencephalon medium divided into terminal plate and roof by the angulus terminalis, the terminology locating the region where the paraphysis arises (ontogeny/terminology); one-page item, no abstract.

'Die epithelialen Gebilde am Gehirn der Wirbeltiere. I' (1922, author unknown): epithelial roof structures could include paraphysis/dorsal sac/plexus; resolve by reading the Springer first page or author/section list.

Hines 1923 development of the Sphenodon telencephalon (telencephalon medium, lamina terminalis, tela) with a possible paraphysis outpocketing (sources conflict); locates the paraphysis in reptile ontogeny; verify passage.

Holmgren and van der Horst 1925 Neoceratodus brain morphology: generic title, no excerpt; resolve by checking whether it describes the roof structure anterior to the velum (paraphysis/dorsal sac) in the lungfish.
Kappers 1929 general 'Evolution of the nervous system' book; library record only, no paraphysis content identified.
Fulton and Bailey 1929 introduced 'neuroepithelial cyst' ending the paraphyseal-origin theory for third-ventricle colloid cysts (per Niknejad 2015); title identification inferred; second-hand.

Byrom and Russell 1932 ependymal cyst of the third ventricle: early ependymal-origin interpretation set against the paraphysial theory, needed to weigh the hypothesis (clinical origin); case report, content unverified.

Kappers, Huber and Crosby 1936 treatise: standard reference whose paraphysis coverage is unknown from the record; resolve by an index check for paraphysis/telencephalon medium in vol. 2 (same work as R042).
Duplicate catalogue entry of the 1936 Kappers/Huber/Crosby treatise; paraphysis chapter/page not identified; resolve by index check.
Gladstone and Wakeley 1940 The Pineal Organ: passages describe the paraphysis and dorsal sac across urodeles (tubular or branched glandular diverticulum), reptiles, crocodilians and mammals.
Same monograph as R043 (UNSW section pages): dorsal sac and paraphysis present in alligator, positions between parietal organ and pineal sac at 25 mm.
Handbuch Bd 6/4 chapter 'Die Epiphysis cerebri' (human pineal); no paraphysis content in the record.

Rudebeck 1945 forebrain morphology in Dipnoi (detailed Protopterus telencephalon development): may describe the roof and paraphysis/coronarium, but title is generic and no excerpt; resolve by checking its roof/velum section.
